questions.q: What is the main job of ColumnTransformer?
options: Train several models and average their predictions
Apply a different preprocessing recipe to different groups of columns and reassemble the result
Split a dataset into train and test sets
questions.explain: You declare (name, transformer, columns) triples, and it applies each recipe to its columns and stitches the outputs together.

questions.q: You pass only the categorical recipe to ColumnTransformer and leave remainder at its default. What happens to the numeric columns?
questions.explain: The default is remainder='drop', so any column you do not list disappears from the output. Use passthrough only when you mean it.

questions.q: Why set handle_unknown='ignore' on OneHotEncoder in a production pipeline?
options: It lets a category unseen in training become all zeros instead of raising an error
It removes rare categories from the training data
questions.explain: With the default setting, a new category at scoring time raises an error. 'ignore' encodes it as all zeros so the job keeps running.

questions.q: In the lesson, the transformed training set had 11 columns. Where did they come from?
options: 4 numeric, plus 3 plan indicators and 4 region indicators
11 numeric columns in the original table
One column per row in the test set
questions.explain: Four numeric columns pass through the imputer and scaler; plan has 3 categories and region has 4, so one-hot encoding adds 3 and 4 columns.

questions.q: Which call recovers readable column names from a fitted ColumnTransformer output?
questions.explain: get_feature_names_out() returns names prefixed with each recipe's name, such as num__age or cat__plan_basic. The transformed output itself is a plain array.
